collection.description: A child has found a pretty orange stone on the beach, and an adult sees that it is a lavastone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found a pretty orange stone on the beach and has been carrying it around all morning. (friend) takes one look and recognizes it: it's a small lavastone, faintly warm, faintly glowing. Nobody knows what a lavastone might do to a child. (subject) is holding it very tightly and looking up at (friend) with enormous eyes.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (friend) kneels down and explains, gently, that this stone is a bit special, and that grown-ups need to look after it until they know more. "But I found it," says (subject). "You did," says (friend), "and that makes you very lucky." (friend.He/She) gives (subject) a beautiful shell in exchange, and lets (subject.him/her) choose where the lavastone should be kept. (subject) chooses a high shelf. (subject.He/She) checks on it every day.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (friend) lets (subject) keep it for now, but watches closely. Nothing happens. The stone stays faintly warm. (subject) sleeps with it, plays with it, talks to it. After a week, it goes cold and dull, and (subject) is very upset, until (friend) points out that it might just be asleep. (subject) wraps it carefully in a leaf, so it can sleep better.
